title: How to Keep Sweat Off Your Controller
brief: Practical ways to keep your hands and controller dry and clean during a sweaty session, like towels, grips and cleaning after.
scene: A generic unbranded game controller on a small towel, with a pair of workout gloves and a spray bottle nearby.

title: Which Game Settings to Change Before You Work Out
brief: In game settings that make games easier to play while moving, like bigger text, subtitles, aim assist, easier difficulty and turning off screen shake.
scene: A big screen showing an abstract settings menu made of plain sliders and toggles with no writing, and a generic controller in the foreground.

title: Headphones or Speakers for Treadmill Gaming?
brief: Compare headphones, earbuds and speakers for gaming over a noisy treadmill or bike. Cover comfort, sweat, wires and hearing your surroundings.
scene: A pair of generic wireless headphones and a small speaker side by side next to the front of a home treadmill.

title: How to Make Your Treadmill Quieter for Gaming
brief: Ways to cut treadmill noise so you can hear your game and not annoy anyone, like mats, maintenance, placement and slower speeds. Follow the manual for maintenance.
scene: A home treadmill on a thick rubber mat in an apartment room, with simple soft sound waves fading out.

title: Can You Stream PC Games to a TV in Front of Your Treadmill?
brief: How to play PC games on a TV near the treadmill using Steam Link, a long cable or a small PC. Cover wired versus wifi and input lag in general terms.
scene: A desktop PC in one room connected by a simple dotted line to a large TV in front of a home treadmill in another room.

title: How to Stay Motivated to Exercise With Video Games
brief: Simple habits for sticking with it, like saving a favorite game for workouts only, picking a set time and starting small. No made up study results.
scene: A wall calendar with simple check marks, a pair of sneakers and a generic controller on a shelf together.

title: How to Keep Cool During Long Gaming Workouts
brief: Fans, water, room temperature, clothes and taking breaks. Tell people to stop if they feel dizzy or unwell. No medical numbers.
scene: A floor fan aimed at a home exercise bike, with a water bottle and a towel, and a TV showing a colorful abstract game.

title: Should You Play Multiplayer Games While You Exercise?
brief: The tradeoffs of online multiplayer on a treadmill or bike, like not being able to pause, needing quick reactions, and which modes work better.
scene: A person on an exercise bike with a generic controller, facing a screen split into two abstract game views.

title: How to Set Up an Exercise Bike for Gaming
brief: The bike version of our treadmill setup guide. Cover screen height, seat position, controller, and why a bike is easier for precise inputs.
scene: A person pedaling a stationary exercise bike holding a generic controller, looking at a TV at eye level in a simple room.

title: Couch Co-op on a Treadmill: Does It Work?
brief: Playing local co-op with one person exercising and one on the couch, or both on machines. Cover which kinds of games fit and how to set it up.
scene: One person walking on a treadmill and another relaxing on a couch, both holding generic controllers and facing the same TV.

title: What to Do if Gaming on a Treadmill Makes You Dizzy
brief: General tips if moving while watching a screen feels off, like slowing down, moving the screen, turning off motion blur and picking other games. Stop if you feel unwell, and see a doctor if it keeps happening.
scene: A treadmill console with a slow speed setting symbol, a person's feet standing still on the side rails, and a calm abstract game on a screen.

title: Handheld, Console or PC for Workout Gaming?
brief: Compare playing on a handheld, a console or a PC while exercising. Cover setup effort, screens, game libraries and pausing.
scene: A generic handheld gaming device, a generic game console and a generic desktop PC lined up on a plain surface, all unbranded.

title: What to Do With Your Game When Your Workout Ends
brief: How to fit gaming into a workout with a clear end, like pause friendly games, save points, timers and cooling down rather than stopping suddenly.
scene: A simple kitchen timer, a generic controller and a towel on a bench next to an exercise bike.

title: Walking Pads vs Treadmills for Gaming
brief: Compare a walking pad and a full treadmill for gaming. Cover space, speed, handrails, safety and noise, in general terms with no invented product specs.
scene: A flat walking pad next to a full size home treadmill, both empty, with a TV on the wall.
